why: bal.118.cau3 बिनु बानी बकता बड़ जोगी: the entry has only 'योगी | yogi'; one reading takes बड़ जोगी as 'बहुत योग्य, कुशल' (able, skilled). Whether to add the sense 'योग्य, कुशल | able, skilled' is not settled (the writer recorded it as disputed).

bal.156.do156 चपरि चलेउ हय सुटुकि नृप: the writer proposes 'चाबुक लगाकर, सटकाकर | with a flick of the whip' beside 'सरपट | darting'. Platts gives saṭak 'a switch, cane' but saṭaknā / suṭuknā only as 'to vanish, run away' (and suṭuknā 'to gulp down'); no dictionary at hand gives the whipping sense for the verb, so it is not settled.

bal.10.cha1 गति कूर कबिता सरित की: the writer proposes 'टेढ़ा, बेढंगा | rough, crooked' for the course of the river of poetry. Platts kūr gives only 'pitiless, cruel, savage'; MW and Apte krūra give 'hard, rough, harsh' but not 'crooked'. Which sense to add ('कठोर, खुरदरी' or 'टेढ़ी') is not settled.

bal.245.cau3 तोरेहुँ धनुषु ब्याहु अवगाहा: the reviewer proposes 'कठिन, दुर्लभ | hard to attain' (the marriage is hard to win even after the bow is broken). MW and Apte give ava-gāha only as 'plunging, bathing' (Platts likewise; the entry already has 'अथाह | unfathomable'); the figurative sense is from context, not from a dictionary, so whether it belongs in the entry is not settled.

issue: ‘मेरी बिरद संभारो’: बिरद is usually the Lord’s own renown (his pledge to save the fallen), ‘अपनी बिरद’; the text has मेरी.
‘मुझसे बिरले बुधवारे हो’ (brahma-aarti pad 4) is unclear; perhaps a corruption of समुझे (‘few wise men understand it’).
as मुझसे: the phrase’s sense is uncertain.
‘जेष्टानन्द बन्द’ (brihaspati-aarti pad 6): बन्द read as वन्द (bows); perhaps a corrupt कन्द.
‘तेल चटकि दधि मिश्रित भाषावलि तेरी’: as printed ‘string of words’; the offering context suggests माषावलि (a row of urad, i.e. vadas fried in oil and soaked in curd).
not a word; read as चतुर्वर्तिका (four-wicked), a dropped repha.
shanidev-aarti pad 4: Śiva, or the poet’s signature.
one word in Drik Panchang; नग + दात is a guess (yashoda-lala-aarti pad3).
= कुमकुमा (saffron; saffron water, or the lac globe of coloured water thrown at festivals).
अतुलित अहि अघ मूषक-भक्षक (natvar-aarti pad4) found nowhere independent; 'eater of a mouse' fits the line poorly.
our sense: devourer of a mouse (Kṛṣṇa swallowing Agha the serpent like a mouse)

issue: दस्यु जियो मारी (narsingh-aarti pad2): जियो unclear; read as जिय (life).
शशिकान्त is the moonstone or the night lotus in MW; the line needs the moon.
आधा नील पीत पटसारी (yugal-kishor-aarti pad6): पट + सारी (robe and sari) or पट सारी (all the garments); the Budhwar recension has ओढ़े नील पीत पट सारी.
our sense: robe and sari (half in a blue sari, half in a yellow robe)

issue: राधिका चमक रही आली (kunj-bihari-aarti pad1): सखी (address) or आलि 'row, line'.
दुन्दुभि बाजत बहु जात (yashoda-lala-aarti pad3): बहु जात 'of many kinds' (जाति) or बाजत जात 'keep sounding'.
बजावै मुरली मधुर बाला (kunj-bihari-aarti pad1): the lad (Kṛṣṇa); the sa entry (the ignorant) does not fit; a hi entry बाला 'the lad' may be better than a sense added to sa.
sitaram-aarti pad4: the poet's name (signature) or Śiva (Rāmeśvara) addressed; see docs/reviews/sitaram-aarti-doubts.jsonl.

giridhari-aarti pad9 (नारायण शरणागत अति अघ … चाहत चितहारी): with the third-person चाहत, नारायण reads as the poet's signature (the poet Nārāyaṇa); the entry has only the Lord. The sense fits this work only, so it belongs in its own glossary.
our sense: नारायण (इस आरतीके कवि) / Nārāyaṇa (the poet of this āratī)

issue: banke-bihari-aarti pad4 (श्री हरि दास के प्यारे तुम हो): हरि दास, printed as two words, is Svāmī Haridāsa of Vṛndāvana, through whom Bāṅke Bihārī was revealed; the entries हरि and दास give only Hari and servant. A work-glossary sense is needed.
our sense: (श्री हरि दास) स्वामी हरिदास, वृन्दावनके संत / Svāmī Haridāsa, the saint of Vṛndāvana

issue: krishna-kanhaiya-aarti pad4: the word is unattested and has one witness (see docs/reviews/krishna-kanhaiya-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
our sense: ईश्वर, स्वामी (perhaps जगेस, lord of the world)

issue: lakshmi-narayan-aarti pad1: the vocative can be of नीरदकान्ति (bahuvrīhi, m.: Viṣṇu, whose lustre is a rain cloud's) or of नीरद-कान्ता (f.: Lakṣmī, the beloved of the cloud-dark Lord). We follow the stanza pattern of pad2 (odd lines Lakṣmī, even lines Viṣṇu).
our sense: हे बादल-जैसी साँवली कान्तिवाले! / O you whose lustre is that of a rain cloud

issue: satyanarayan-aarti pad3: not found in Platts; read as कठहारा (wood-gatherer), the woodcutter of the Satyanārāyaṇa story.
giridhari-aarti pad5: read as मंजारी, f. of मंजार (Platts), Skt मार्जारी, a cat (the cat whose kittens were saved in the potter's kiln).
"अघ मोघ क्षमाकर": मोघ = vain/fruitless; the phrase likely means one who makes sins fruitless (or a corruption of मोचक)
"हरहु नेष्ट ग्रह": not a dictionary word; read as अनिष्ट
"वप्र आदि कोणस्थ": वप्र (rampart) does not fit; read as बभ्रु, Śani's name in his name-list (कोणस्थ, पिंगल, बभ्रु …)
"पिप्पल तन साजा": pipal tree or Śani's name Pippalāda
"ललत स्वर्ण पद करत निहाला": not in Platts; read as ललित
"घोर रौद्रतन अघमन काला": unclear; read as अघ-मर्दन
"त्रैल तेश है नाम तुम्हारा" (with तेश): likely a split त्रैलतेश = त्रैलोकेश, lord of the three worlds
a Bhairava name not found in the dictionaries; taken literally
"क्षेत्रपाल दसपाण कहाये": read as दशपाणि (ten-handed); not found as written
a Bhairava name, not found in the dictionaries
"कारण लम्ब आप भय भंजन": unclear; taken as लम्ब (tall), a name
"आपहि वारे छीजन धाये": unclear (वाले? बालक?)
"छीजन धाये": taken as a place name; not in Platts
"गये हिवारे मैं": taken as a village name (Hivārā)
not in Platts; read as झब्बा (tassel)
"सफल एक ते एक सिवाये": सिवाय = beyond, more
"साद भक्त को कारज सार्यो": a devotee's name or साधु
"पावन सुखद मनन अनरूपा": read as अनुरूप
"पावन चरण भवोभव कारी": unclear; read as भव-उद्भव
"मनु मय त्वष्टा शिल्पी महाना । देवागम …": the five sons of Viśvakarmā are Manu, Maya, Tvaṣṭā, Śilpī, Daivajña; read as दैवज्ञ
"रक्तबीज शंखन संहारे": Śaṅkhāsura (a demon) or a plural
"करेंगी शोषण-पार्वती माँ": शोषण (draining) does not fit; the usual text reads "पोषण पार्वती माँ"
"चौंसठ योगिनी-भैरों बरवन": read as बावन (the 52 Bhairavas)
"जाह्नवी अरु उत्राणी": not found; a name of the Goddess (इन्द्राणी? उत्तराणी?)
"पाटन मुम्बा दन्त कुमारी": unclear (Dantesvarī? Kanyākumārī?)
"पवन रूप हो गई प्रवीणा": प्रवीण = skilled; the line seems to need "vanished" (perhaps प्रविलीन)
‘पतिदेवता सुतीत शिरोमनि’: सुतीत is not a word; read as सुतिय/सुती (good wife; Platts: su-tiya-maṇi, an epithet of Pārvatī).
our sense: a virtuous wife (crest-jewel of devoted wives)

issue: ‘अज-अनवद्य अनंत अपूर्णे’: अपूर्णे (incomplete) cannot be a praise; likely अपर्णे (Aparṇā, Pārvatī) or अपूर्वे.
‘राज हंस तुम्हारो शचि वाहन’: शचि (Śacī, Indra's wife) does not fit; read as शुचि (pure).
‘महिमा अमित अथाह अर्पणा । ब्रह्म हरि हर मात अर्पणा’: perhaps अपर्णा (Pārvatī) in both; perhaps ‘offered’ in the second.
‘कमल कान्तिमय शान्ति अनपा’: read as अनूपा (unequalled).
‘जोतमन मर्यादा जोत स्वरुपा’: read as ज्योतिर्मय (full of light); the line is garbled.
‘सिद्ध योगिनी सहस्या राजे’: read as सहस्र (thousands).
‘भद्र काली कम्पलेश्वर आई’: not identified (a place or a Śiva shrine near the Śākambharī dhām?).
‘अद्भुत चंचल चित्त चितेरी’: Platts चितेरा = painter; the sense is perhaps ‘one who paints (charms) the restless mind’.
‘कान्त शाकम्भरी अति सुखदाई’, ‘कान्त शिवा भगतन सुखदाई’: taken as the poet Kāntā Prasāda's signature (he names himself in cau ‘कान्ता प्रसाद जगाधरी वासी’); could be ‘lovely’.
‘श्री शीतला शेढ़ला महला । रुणलीह्युणनी मातु मंदला’: folk names of Śītalā, the second garbled; perhaps Ruṇakī-Jhuṇakī. महला and मंदला not checked in a dictionary.
‘पुरी तिवारी मोर निवासा’: a village (Tivārīpur?) or the poet's surname.
‘पड़ा क्षर तव आस लगाई’: perhaps ‘(this) perishable one lies …’; perhaps a misprint of द्वार (at your door).
‘दीन्हो श्राप कध पर आनी’: कध is not a word; perhaps क्रोध (bringing anger) or कंध.
‘समय पाई व्हौ रौ पाती तोरा’: garbled; the sense is ‘in time I shall be your husband’ (व्हौ = होऊँगा; रौ unclear, पाती = पति).
‘धग्व रूप हम शालिग्रामा’: read as धरब (I shall take).
‘आशिय धन जन लड़हि ग्रह बसही पूर्णा अत्र’: garbled; read as लहहि (obtain); आशिय as आशिष.
‘जई पगु सुरसरि हेतु उठावहि । तइ जगि अश्वमेध फल पावहि’: read as जितने … उतने … यज्ञ (as many steps, so many horse-sacrifices).
‘पूरण चालीसा कियो हरि भक्तन हित नैत्र’ (rhymes with चैत्र): नेत्र (eyes)? The sense of the half-line is unclear.
Gaṅgā's netherworld stream is usually Bhogavatī; the text says प्रभावति.
‘धरयौ मातु पुनि काशी करवट’: the Gaṅgā's northward turn at Kāśī, or the holy spot ‘Kāśī-karavaṭ’.
‘रक्त बीज काटा रण मुण्डी’: perhaps ‘the goddess with the garland of heads’ (Cāmuṇḍā); the sa entry has only ‘shaven-headed’.
not in Platts; read as निशा-तम (perhaps a misprint): 'remove the darkness of night, make light'
our sense: (अज्ञानरूपी) रातका अँधेरा / the darkness of night (of ignorance)

issue: 'भक्तवृन्द तेहिं जांचा': जाँचना = beg (याच) or test; both given
form not found in Platts; read as उछल-उछल (leaping for joy)
Platts sakaṛ = sakal; read with सकड़ा (packed tight) in 'सकड़ भीड़'
not in Platts; Rajasthani छीड़ = room, open space ('no room')
'देश देश में भव भौति है': not in Platts; read as Rajasthani भौत = बहुत, with भव as glory/honour; the line is unclear
'हाथ पसारि लीन्ह चौगानी': Platts has only चौगानी = a ḥuqqa tube; read from चौगान (open ground): openly, before all
not in Platts; read as कु + बड़ाई (ill report)
'माम सिकन्दर के तुम मारा': no fitting sense; read as a misprint for मान (pride)
the disciple named beside Mīrā is not identified (the Jhālī queen?)
Gaṅgārāma chālīsā 'महावीर धर ध्यान पुनीता । विरचेउ…': read as the poet's name; could be 'meditating on Mahāvīra (Hanumān)'
'दिन दोपारा दूर परैं' (Gaṇpati kī sevā, pad 3) is obscure; read as 'midday had passed / it was midday'
'पगथंभा सा उदर पुष्ट है': read as पग + थंभा (pillar-like legs), beside a stout belly
Ravidāsa chālīsā 'बंदीगृह काटी है रानी': queen makes no sense; read as रैनि (night): 'passed the night in prison'
our sense: रात (रैनि), proposed as an added sense

issue: 'जात जडूला रात जगावे' (Rāṇī Satī): read as Rajasthani jāt (vowed pilgrimage to the family goddess) beside jaḍūlā (first tonsure)
our sense: जात (कुलदेवीके दर्शनकी मनौती-यात्रा), proposed as an added sense

issue: "अका बका" in krishna-chalisa cau12; अका is taken as Aghāsura (अघ), killed with Baka; spelling unusual
"पिता कियो मारन परसाया" (narasimha-chalisa cau7) rhymes with दासा; taken as a corruption of प्रयासा (attempt)
narasimha-chalisa do1 names कृतिका (Kṛttikā) with Vaiśākha śukla caturdaśī; Narasiṃha Jayantī is usually tied to Svātī; the entry glosses the word as printed
"ललहिं चारि फल शरण तुम्हारी" (parashurama-chalisa cau38): no such verb; taken as लहहिं (obtain), probably a misprint
"सविता हंस सुनूर विभाकर" (surya-chalisa cau2): not found in Platts or MW; taken as a name of the Sun ("of fair light")
our sense: of fair light (a name of the Sun)

issue: "सविता सूर्य अर्क खग कलिकर" (surya-chalisa cau9): not found; given only as a name of the Sun
"रिपु सों जमलहते सोतेहि छन" (surya-chalisa cau16): read as जम लहते (foes meet Yama, die) at that very moment; text may be corrupt
"कंठ सुवर्ण रेत की शोभा" (surya-chalisa cau22): read as the name Suvarṇaretas split over two words
"भानुमान उरसर्म सुउदरचन" (surya-chalisa cau24): read as Bhānumān guarding (शर्म) the chest and the belly; सुउदरचन unclear, perhaps corrupt
our sense: guard of the chest / guards the belly

issue: "यम भादों आश्विन हिमरेता" (surya-chalisa cau39): a month-name of the Sun; not found (perhaps for हिरण्यरेता)
our sense: a name of the Sun (in Āśvina)

issue: "हे रवि सुव्रन" (shanishchar-chalisa so1): taken as सुवन (son), "son of the Sun"
"कानन किला शिविर सेनाकर" (shanishchar-chalisa cau8): no such word; read as armies (सेना + आकर)
"इकहोइ धारण करत शनि नित । वंदत सोई शनि को दमनचित" (shanishchar-chalisa cau27): unclear; read as "being one-pointed … with mind subdued"
"रेणुका नयना नन्दं" (parashurama-chalisa shloka1) is नयनानन्दम् split by the print: entries give नयना = eyes, नन्दं = joy-giver
"पूर्ण इन्द्र अरविन्द मुख" (krishna-chalisa do2): इन्द्र reads as a misprint of इन्दु (moon); proposed sense added
"अज विधि घाता नाम" (brahma-chalisa do2): घाता reads as a misprint of धाता (creator); proposed sense added
"सरयू तोर सहित अनुरागा" (shanishchar-chalisa cau16): तोर probably for तीर (bank); proposed sense added
"अगहन भिन्न विष्णु हैं पूसहिं" (surya-chalisa cau40): भिन्न probably a misprint of मित्र (Mitra, the Sun of Agahan); entry left unchanged
"अस जोजन अपने मन माहीं" / "जोजन याको मनमहं जापै" (surya-chalisa): जोजन = जो जन (whoever), not yojana; proposed sense added

These Awadhi words currently fall back to Sanskrit entries whose senses do not fit (भो 'O!', करौ 'the two hands', भान्ति 'shine'); new awa entries are proposed in add.awa (beyond the todo's missing list) so Awadhi verses stop reaching the Sanskrit senses
The English sense 'jew's harp' (Platts: 'a jew's harp') is a dated name many now find offensive; the meaning of kunj-bihari-aarti stanza 2 now says 'mouth harp'.
suggestion: en: 'mouth harp (jaw harp), a small instrument played at the mouth'

issue: a name of the Goddess in a list (kali-chalisa cau3); MW/Apte give halā = earth, water, wine, or a vocative to a female friend; which sense the name has is unclear
जाया can be 'wife' or 'born/begot'; the line (कात्यायनी उमा जगजाया) allows 'mother of the world' or 'wife of the Lord of the world'
our sense: जगत्‌को जन्म देनेवाली / जगत्पति शिवजीकी पत्नी

issue: in a list of names: could be महा+तम 'great darkness' or a spelling of महात्मा
'सिद्धि कवि हिन्द' in the closing doha: whether हिन्द is the poet's pen-name or 'of India' is unclear
'स्वछन्द रद मारद धुनि माही' (mahakali-chalisa) is obscure; मारद may be a corrupt spelling (मार+द 'slaying', or मार्दल 'drum')
onomatopoeic sounds in 'झननन तच्छु मरिरिन नादिनि'; no dictionary sense
compound in 'तू ब्रह्माण्डे शक्तिजितचण्डे' can be split several ways
unusual forms; -अयनि read as 'abode' for कमलायनि and as a mere extension of श्यामा
'धूम्र विलोचनि प्राण विमोचनि' read as 'who took the life of Dhūmralocana'; split across two words
'सकल काज भक्तन के सरनी': read as सारनी (accomplisher, from सारना); could also be a spelling of शरणी (refuge)
'पुरवहु आशन करहु अबारी': no clear dictionary form; Platts has abār 'near bank' and bār 'delay'; read as 'now, without delay'
'बुद्धि विपरीत भई खलहाला' (saraswati-chalisa): obscure; read as 'of the wicked ones'
'कानन में घेरे मृग नाहै': read as मृग-नाह 'lord of beasts' (lion), Platts nāh = lord
'गोविंद निशदिन शरण तिहारी' (mahalakshmi-chalisa): likely the poet's name (signature line), possibly the Lord
'स्थित रक्षा लय हित सजाता' (parvati-chalisa): सजाता may stand for सृजता / रचती; the line is loose
'श्री चन्द्रेश्वरि नैमिष प्यारा' (lalita-chalisa): name of the Goddess at Naimiṣa; not found as a standard epithet
'होवे सुख आनन्द अधीसा': read as अधीश (lord) — 'becomes master of joy' — or as 'abundant' for the rhyme
'तुम्हीं शारदा चक्र-कपाली': not a standard epithet; read as bearer of discus and skull
'कपर्दिनी कलि कल्प बिमोचनि' (mahakali-chalisa): कल्प may stand for कल्मष (sins of the Kali age); the entry's senses (aeon / wish-tree) do not clearly fit; no sense added
'देव मगन के हित अस कीन्हों' (parvati-chalisa): मगन may be a misprint for देवगन (the gods); the entry's 'absorbed' does not clearly fit; no sense added
'मम सन तरैं पातकी भारी': added sense 'like' (मम सन = like me); the entry has से / साथ only
ramdev-aarti pad 3 ‘सरजीवन भाण को तुमने कर डारा’: who Bhāṇ is was not found (the Rāmdev Chālīsā's revivals are a merchant, Sugnā's son, Bakhśī's son); possibly a name, possibly भाणेज (sister's son).
our sense: Bhāṇ, a name: one whom Rāmdev brought back to life

issue: baba-gangaram-aarti pad 1 ‘जो उनके सारो काम’: सारो as Rajasthani सारना (accomplish) gives the line its verb; as सारा (all) the line has none.
jaharveer-aarti refrain ‘जय जय जाहरवीर हरे’ imitates ‘जय जगदीश हरे’ (vocative of हरि); could also be read ‘who removes (sorrow)’.
our sense: O Hari (Jāharvīr addressed as the Lord)

issue: jaharveer-aarti pad 6 ‘भवन पधारो अटल क्षत्र कह’: क्षत्र read as छत्र (royal canopy); could be क्षत्रिय or क्षेत्र. The line's syntax is loose.
our sense: canopy (‘O unshakeable canopy’, the sovereign protector)

issue: jaharveer-aarti pad 5: read as मढ़ी (an ascetic's hut, small shrine; cf. Gogāmeṛī); Platts's माड़ी (rice-water, palm) do not fit.
rani-sati-aarti pad 4 ‘सुरगम ध्यान धरे’: read as सुरगण (hosts of gods); not otherwise a word (सरगम ‘musical scale’ would not take ध्यान धरे).
rani-sati-aarti pad 7: not a known compound; read as सदन + सिद्धि (success in the home); perhaps a corruption of सदा सिद्धि or अष्टसिद्धि.
rani-sati-aarti pad 1 ‘अपनि अनन्तर ज्योति’: taken in MW's sense ‘uninterrupted, continuous’ (with अखण्डित); could stand for अनन्त (endless) or आन्तर (inner).
rani-sati-aarti pad 5 ‘सेवक जन हृदय पटले मृदुल करन सुमति’: पटल (surface, screen) + locative; the line's construction is loose.
मेवा अरू मिष्ठान प्रवीना: प्रवीण is 'skilled'; here it seems to qualify the sweets ('choice, fine'), or loosely 'of every kind'
रामानन्द सदा सुख सन्दन: सन्दन is not a common word; read as सदन ('abode') for the rhyme with भंजन (स्यन्दन 'chariot' does not fit)
तिमिर मय जग कीन्हो तीन्हा: read as तीनों (लोक), 'the three worlds'; it may be a rhyme-form of कीन्हा
अति आतुर यम कातर तोरा (Bajrang Bāṇ): यमकातर is a dagger (Yama's knife) by the usual reading; कातर 'frightened' is the other reading
अमिलख असुरन द्वन्द मचाया (Vishnu Chālīsā): not a word; read as अमिय लखि ('seeing the nectar')
कूर्म रूप धर सिन्धु मझाया: probably मथाया ('had churned'); मझाना 'to go into the middle' is the other reading
देखत तीन दनुज शैतानी: तीन 'three' does not fit the Jalandhara story; perhaps तिन ('him, them')
देहि सकल बाँछित फल शीशा (Gopāla Chālīsā): शीशा 'head' does not fit; perhaps ईशा ('the Lord gives') or 'on the head'
डासना पी नित कृपा तुम्हारी (Maṅgalamaya Gaṇeśa Chālīsā): the existing entry पी is 'beloved (husband)'; the line wants 'on' (पै), or the half is a slip for दासन पर (see the work's doubts)
उनके तुम साथी गौरीसा: addressed to Gaṇeśa, but गौरीश is Śiva (Gaurī's lord); perhaps meant for गौरीसुत or a vocative 'O (son of) Gaurī's lord'
our sense: entry kept as शिव; the verse meaning must decide

issue: अग्नि बैताल काल मारी मर (Bajrang Bāṇ): मारी मर read as मारी, मरी 'plague, pestilence'; मर 'dies' is the other reading
हार पार शिव सकल बनाई (Vishnu Chālīsā): हार and पार unclear in the Jalandhara story; perhaps 'Śiva was all but defeated'
shitala-aarti pad9 उत्पत्ति बाला बिनाशन: बाला ('girl') fits poorly in a list of creation and destruction; पाला/पालन or वाला ('the one of') are possible; see docs/reviews/shitala-aarti-doubts.jsonl
our sense: Bālā, the maiden (the Goddess as a young girl)

issue: sharda-aarti pad3 कंधे से विनय सुनाऊँ: 'from the shoulders' is obscure; कंठ से ('from the throat') is a possible original
sharda-aarti pad4 कर्ण को टीका: 'a ṭīkā of the ear' is obscure; कर्म ('deeds') is a possible original
tulsi-aarti pad1 सब योगों के ऊपर: योग may be the spiritual disciplines or (beside रोगों, रुज) medicinal preparations
sharda-aarti do1 धरो मात अवतार: past (Braj धरो = धरा, 'took') or imperative ('take')
annapurna-aarti pad2 सुर सुरों की रचना: 'gods and the hosts of gods'; सुर-असुरों ('gods and demons') is possible
Not a Sanskrit headword; probably a misprint of सोमोद्भवा (MW: the Narmadā, 'moon-born').
our sense: सोमोद्भवा, चन्द्रमासे उत्पन्न (नर्मदाका नाम) / Somodbhavā, moon-born

issue: 'मातृ-पितृ देव मनजो भावे' — reading unclear: मन जो (whoever in heart) or मनुज जो (the man who).
our sense: मनसे जो (जिसके मनको भाते हैं) / whoever in his heart

issue: 'तीन मण्ड में' and 'मण्ड पे' — not in Platts; taken as मण्डल (realm) and मण्डप (shrine).
'बन्धु छोड़ना इनके चरणाँ' — the line seems to need 'never leave their feet'; a negative may be lost from the text.
'जी ले श्याम नाम के हाले' — Platts has only the interjection हले; taken as हवाले/सहारे.
our sense: सहारे, हवाले / in the care of

issue: 'चिथड़ों का घोड़ा ही साया' — the cloth horse came to life; form unclear (साधा? सजा?).
our sense: सध गया, चल पड़ा / was made to go

issue: 'दूध उफणता चरा उठाया' — Rajasthani चरू (big cooking pot) assumed; not in Platts.
our sense: चरू, बड़ा बर्तन / large cooking pot

issue: Rajasthani परिंडा (water-pot stand); not in Platts.
'निकलंग नाडी सिरजी प्यारी' — taken as निष्कलंक (spotless); could be a form of निकला.
'निजसर जल खारा करवाया' — taken as 'his own pond'; may be a place name.
'परच्या बाईसवां मिर्जो चीहां' — taken as चीन्हा (recognised, tested); uncertain.
Existing entry (पड़ी) does not fit 'परच्या तेरहवां पीर परी पधारया'; the word may be filler or a misprint. No sense proposed.
'भक्त के लिये आज था देव बना प्रतिहारी' — door-keeper/attendant taken; the line may intend प्रतिकारी (avenger) or उपकारी.
'झंझा से झंकृत नैया' — झंकृत is 'jingling, resounding'; the line needs 'tossed, rattled'.
Existing entry: in 'करि कोविद करि सके न गिनन्ता' the first करि is unclear (कोटि? करोड़?); no sense added.
‘हरि ब्रह्मा शिवरी’ (ambe-aarti tek): read as शिव + री (री calling to the Mother); other prints have शिवजी.
‘श्रीमालकेतु में राजत कोटि रतन ज्योति’ (ambe-aarti pad 11): the name is not identified in the dictionaries; taken as a place or seat of the Mother.
our sense: Śrīmālaketu, a seat of the Mother

issue: ‘धूम्र विलोचन नैना निशदिन मदमाती’ (ambe-aarti pad 5): read as the demon Dhūmralocana (slain, carrying on from the line before), then ‘your eyes are ever flushed’; it can also be read as ‘smoke-dark eyes’.
‘सब अपने स्वास्थ के कर्ता’ (chitragupta-aarti pad 7): every witness prints स्वास्थ; स्वारथ (self-interest) would fit better.
‘तेरे ही गुन गायें भारती’ (durga-aarti tek): Sarasvatī (Bhāratī) or the people of Bhārata.
‘प्रभु लंका विजय करावो’ (vishwakarma-aarti pad 3): an imperative form in a list of past deeds; read as past.
jagjanani-aarti pad8: सरुपा is not a standard word; सरूपा or स्वरूपा is likely meant (docs/reviews/jagjanani-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
kushmanda-aarti pad3 सुख पहुँचती हो: पहुँचती does not take सुख as object; पहुँचाती is likely meant (docs/reviews/kushmanda-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
katyayani-aarti pad2: कही ('called') as printed, or कहीं ('somewhere') as DNA Hindi has it (docs/reviews/katyayani-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
jagjanani-aarti pad9: a rare compound, set against स्नेह-सुधामयि; read as 'whose mind is poison', the Goddess fierce and deadly to the wicked.
our sense: विष-जैसे (उग्र) मनवाली / whose mind is like poison

issue: katyayani-aarti pad1: which Baijnāth (Kangra, Himachal; or Vaidyanātha, Deoghar) the āratī means is not said.
our sense: बैजनाथ, एक तीर्थस्थान / Baijnāth, a place of pilgrimage

issue: हिन्दी आरतियोंमें मा (माँ) ये (यह) and पर (on; but) resolve to sa.json, whose senses ('do not', 'those who', 'another (world)') do not fit; written as hi entries rather than added senses of the Sanskrit words.
our sense: माँ / Mother; यह / this; पर / on, but

issue: gau-mata pad4 ‘स्नेह स्वभाव विश्व जैया की’: a rhyme form in -ैया; read as जाया/जननी (from जनना). Platts has no जैया in this sense.
our sense: mother, she who gives birth (the mother of the world)

issue: gau-mata tek: धैया read as धाय/धाई (Platts: wet-nurse, foster-mother), a rhyme form; with the pending हरनि (remover) the line has no stated object.
gau-mata pad3 ‘विवेक बुद्धि दैया की’: read as ‘giver’ (Platts दाई, giver); Platts also has दैया ‘mother’.
narmada tek ‘शिव हरि शंकर रुद्री पालन्ती’: Rudrāṇī (the goddess named with the gods) or Rudra's daughter (the Narmadā as born of Śiva).
narmada pad1 ‘अभिनव पदचण्डी’: no dictionary word; read पद + चण्डी.
narmada pad1: no dictionary word; read पद + वन्दिता (whose feet are worshipped), a rhyme form in -न्ती.
narmada pad2 ‘धूमक वाहन राजत’: not in Platts or MW; read as धूम (pomp, Platts). Could also be a name of her mount or ‘smoke-coloured’.
narmada pad3 ‘बाजत ताल मृदंगा, सुरमण्डल रमती’: the instrument svaramaṇḍala (beside ताल, मृदंग) or the assembly of the gods.
narmada pad3: a sung refrain word; read तोड़ी (the rāga) + तान; Platts also has ‘tān toṛnā’, to break into a tān.
narmada pad3: rhyme form; read सुर = स्वर (melodious); could be सुर = gods (worshipped by gods).
khatu-shyam pad4 ‘शंख मृदंग घुरे’: Platts has घुरना only as घूरना (to stare); the line needs ‘resound’ (cf. घोर, घुर्, roar).

The entry lists the same sense twice: 'पर, ऊपर (परसर्ग: ‘जा पर’, ‘सिर पर’) / पर, ऊपर (परसर्ग) / परन्तु / दूसरा, पराया' — 'on, upon (postposition) / on, upon (postposition) / but / other'. The senses are right; the second 'पर, ऊपर (परसर्ग)' / 'on, upon (postposition)' is a duplicate and should be dropped.
our reading: hi: पर, ऊपर (परसर्ग: ‘जा पर’, ‘सिर पर’) / परन्तु / दूसरा, पराया; en: on, upon (postposition) / but / other

issue: en 'great mountains' is plural; in giriraj pad6 (हम हैं शरण तुम्हारी गिरिवर गिरधारी) it addresses one mountain, Girirāja. The sense added above covers the line; the plural en may be made singular.

raghuvar-aarti pad3: every witness (the book, Drik Panchang, BhaktiBharat) prints अवन्ह and none offers another word; Monier-Williams and Apte give avana 'preserving, a preserver'. Settled: रक्षा करनेवाले / protector. Remove from docs/reviews/dictionary-doubts.jsonl.

janaki-aarti pad3 (सरबस धन हरिचन्द अली की): Platts, अली s.f. 'a woman's female friend (= ālī)'; the poet Haricanda speaks as Sītā's sakhī. Settled: सखी / companion. Remove from docs/reviews/dictionary-doubts.jsonl.

sitaram-aarti pad4: the poet's name (signature, as usual in a last stanza) or Śiva (Rāmeśvara) addressed; no source found names the poet. The meaning addresses 'Rāmeśvara' and reads either way. Still open (docs/reviews/sitaram-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
mahakali-aarti pad3 ‘जब लुँकड़ पर हुकुम करे’: Platts has लौंकड़ा / लौकड़ा, ‘a boy attendant of a goddess’, and लौकड़िया-बीर, an epithet of Bhairava; the Goddess's attendant is commonly called लाँगुर.
our sense: लौंकड़ा, लाँगुर, देवीका बालक सेवक (भैरव) / the Goddess's boy attendant Lāṅgur (Bhairava)

issue: mahakali-aarti pad3 ‘वार शनिश्चर कुंकुम बरणो’: बरण may be वर्ण (colour: vermilion-hued on Saturday) or बरनना (to describe: kumkum is described).
vindhyeshwari-aarti pad3 ‘कलयुग राज सवाया’: सवाया is ‘a quarter more’ (Platts sawāyā = sawaiyā); taken as ‘greater still’ in the Kali age.
our sense: एक-चौथाई अधिक, और भी बढ़कर / a quarter more, greater still

issue: vindhyeshwari-aarti pad2 ‘सुवा चोली’: Platts सुवा adj. = सूहा, red; सुवा is also a parrot (whence parrot-green).
lalita-aarti ‘जय शरणं वरणं नमो नमः’: शरणं वरणं taken as ‘I choose (your) refuge’; वरण can also be ‘protection, covering’.
parvati-aarti pad7 ‘श्री प्रताप आरती मैया की’: read as the poet's signature (docs/reviews/parvati-aarti-doubts.jsonl); the entry has only ‘glory, valour’. A work-glossary sense is needed.
our sense: प्रताप (इस आरतीके कवि) / Pratāp (the poet of this āratī)

issue: mahakali-aarti pad4 ‘आदित वारी आदि भवानी’: वारी read as वार (day): ‘on Sunday’, beside ‘वार शनिश्चर’ (pad3) and ‘मंगल की सेवा’ (Tuesday, refrain) and ‘सात बार की महिमा’ (pad6).
our sense: वार, दिन / day of the week

issue: हनुमत सहितासु गाई: सहित + सु (well) or a slip; one witness (docs/reviews/mangal-murti-hanuman-aarti-doubts.jsonl).
printed as one word; अयन (abode, refuge) + महाकाली is a guess (har-har-mahadev-aarti doubts).
our sense: महाकालीके आश्रय / the abode (refuge) of Mahākālī

issue: हंस + ? ; हंसावलि (a row of swans) possible (gangadhar-aarti doubts).
read as रामः + त्रिजट (Śiva, MW) + नाथम्; who Rāma is (Śrī Rāma, or the poet naming himself) is not certain.
our sense: राम, त्रिजट स्वामीको / Rāma, (bowing to) the lord with matted locks

issue: सङ्गतिम् (union, company) or a slip for सङ्गीतम् (song); the line says whoever recites it daily.
कौशला read as Kosala (Ayodhyā), whose welfare Hanumān reported; Kausalyā is possible.
our sense: कोसलका कुशल-मंगल सुनानेवाले / who told of Kosala's welfare

issue: सुर + भूप: 'gods and kings' (a list with ज्ञानी विज्ञानी) or 'king of the gods' (Indra).
our sense: देवता और राजा / gods and kings

issue: मधुर-सी (sweet, as it were) or मधु-राशि (a mass of sweetness); the rhyme -आसी runs through the āratī.
शिवमुनि मन-हारी: शिव (auspicious) + मुनि-मन-हारी is the likely reading (har-har-mahadev-aarti doubts).
our sense: कल्याणरूप; मुनियोंके (मन हरनेवाले) / auspicious; (captivating) the sages

issue: hi.json has no हर, so it falls back to sa (Śiva); मंगल मूरति pad7 has हर प्राणी 'every creature'. Added a hi entry with both senses rather than add 'every' to sa.json.
falls back to sa तां 'that'; in गंगाधर pad4 it is a dance/drum syllable. Added a hi entry.
falls back to sa कानन 'forest'; in बदरीनाथ pad4 कानन कुण्डल is Braj कानन 'in the ears'. Added a hi entry with both senses.

navagraha-chalisa cau37 (तीरथराज प्रयाग सुपासा): Platts सुपास is 'security, ease, happiness', but the same poet's signature in the Śītalā Chālīsā says तट प्रयाग से पूरब पासा, and Kakarā lies east of Prayāga, not in it: सु + पासा 'close by'. Settled: पास, निकट / near (added as a sense; the 'comfort' sense stays for the Mānas).
navagraha-chalisa cau16 (पूजहु आस दास कहुँ): Platts pūjnā v.n. 'to be filled, fulfilled', pujānā v.t. 'to fill, complete, accomplish'; 'worship' does not fit आस. Settled: पूरी करो / fulfil.

navagraha-chalisa cau15 (रोहिणी नन्दन): the writer asked for 'one who gladdens'; not added. Monier-Williams gives Rauhiṇeya, 'son of Rohiṇī', as a metronymic of the planet Mercury (VarBṛS., Sch.), so रोहिणी नन्दन is that epithet and the existing sense 'son' fits; the meaning now reads 'son of Rohiṇī'.
The entry's English 'brings (across)' does not match its own Hindi 'लगाता है'; in mahalakshmi-chalisa cau32 (ध्यान लगावै) it is 'applies, fixes (the mind)'.
suggestion: check which work needs 'brings (across)'; if none, replace it with 'applies, fixes'

issue: The Hindi 'कल्याण करनेवाले' is masculine/plural for a feminine word; kali-chalisa cau50 and mahakali-chalisa cau5 use it of the Goddess.
suggestion: hi 'कल्याण करनेवाली' (the added sense), or make the first sense feminine

why: The entry's only sense, 'इस चालीसाके रचयिता (कवि) | Lalitā, the poet of this chālīsā', fits one line in the library: shanishchar-chalisa chalisa.do3 (सरस सुभाषा में वही ललिता लिखें सुधार). It is wrong for lalita-chalisa cau29, cau41, cau48 (the Goddess; that work's poet is Jitendra Chandra Bhāratīya, cau46): the Goddess sense is added here. The poet sense, used by one work only, should move from awa.json to shanishchar-chalisa's own glossary.json (PLAYBOOK §5).

issue: The shared entry's second sense, 'प्रताप, इस आरतीके कवि / Pratāpa, the poet of this āratī', belongs to one work only (parvati-aarti stanza 7); it is now in tools/works/parvati-aarti/glossary/hi.json.
suggestion: Remove that sense from library/glossary/hi.json, leaving 'प्रताप, तेज | glory, valour'.

issue: The shared entry's second sense, 'चन्द्र (इस चालीसाके रचयिता कवि) / Candra (the poet of this chālīsā)', belongs to mahavir-chalisa alone (chaupāī 36, चालीसे को चन्द्र बनावे; its README names the poet so); lalita-chalisa chaupāī 46 has चन्द्र as part of the poet's name Jitendra Chandra Bhāratīya. In a shared entry 'this chālīsā' is wrong for every other work (gopal-chalisa chaupāī 18: शरद चन्द्र, the autumn moon). Proposal: drop the poet sense from library/glossary/awa.json and give it to tools/works/mahavir-chalisa/glossary/awa.json (and lalita-chalisa's, as part of the name), owned by those works' reviewers.

gopal-chalisa chaupāī 41 (देहि सकल बाँछित फल शीशा): the entry's 'सिर / head' is the plain reading, kept in the meaning; the reading as ईश, 'the Lord', is in docs/reviews/gopal-chalisa-doubts.jsonl. No change to the entry.
